bugs: Duplicate SKUs within a single 500-row chunk are collapsed by keying $valid on sku (app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:133), so the extra rows are counted in total_rows but not in created, updated or failed. Probe: 3 rows (A1, A1, B) gave total=3, created=2, updated=0, failed=0. The test test_duplicate_sku_in_file_keeps_last_row only asserts created+updated==1, so it hides the gap.
Stock has no upper bound, so 99999999999 passes validation for an unsignedInteger column (ProcessImport.php:123). On MySQL the upsert throws and the whole job fails instead of recording a row error.
POST returns 200 instead of 201, because $import->fresh() loses wasRecentlyCreated (ImportController.php:27).
On retry after a mid-run crash, products upserted in the earlier attempt are counted as 'updated' instead of 'created'.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:53: the queued job depends on an HTTP FormRequest constant (StoreImportRequest::REQUIRED_COLUMNS). The domain constant belongs on the model or CsvReader.
app/Http/Requests/StoreImportRequest.php:31: app(CsvReader::class) service-located inside after(), with manual fopen/fclose even though CsvReader already has a header() helper.
app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:17: abort_if(503) for a store() failure is ceremony.
app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:124: custom attribute names mapped to themselves (['sku'=>'sku',...]) do nothing useful.
tests/Feature/ProductImportTest.php:26: Http::preventStrayRequests() is irrelevant here, and inline FQCN \App\Imports\CsvReader is used in tests.
strengths: Uses LazyCollection streaming with chunk() and a bulk Product::upsert. This scales to 5MB files within the timeout.
Raises queue retry_after to 360 to match Timeout(300), and adds FailOnTimeout, so a long import is not run twice.
Stores failure_reason. Missing columns fail the job immediately through $this->fail() with no pointless retries.
Validates the header in the FormRequest after() hook, handling BOM, header case and column order.
Uses modern attributes throughout (#[Fillable], #[WithoutTimestamps], queue attributes), enum casts, and route ->can() authorization with an auto-discovered policy.
Has a unique (import_id,row) index and orders errors explicitly in show.
Tests are thorough (BOM, CRLF, short rows, fractional stock, idempotency, re-run of a processing import, mail content).

bugs: The 202 response from POST returns total_rows/created/updated/failed as null, because the model is not refreshed after create and the DB defaults are not loaded (ImportController.php:29). Confirmed by probe.

Each row runs updateOrCreate, which is 2–3 queries per row (ProcessProductImport.php:75). A full 5MB file (~100k rows) can approach Timeout(300). The default database queue retry_after (90s) is shorter than the timeout, so a long import can be picked up and processed again while still running.
A missing-columns header in the job throws RuntimeException and is retried 3 times with backoff even though the failure is deterministic. No failure reason is stored on the import.
All row errors are buffered in memory until the end of the file. On a mid-run crash, any partial progress on errors is lost.
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:17 and app/Policies/ImportPolicy.php:10: Gate::authorize('create') against a policy that always returns true is ceremony.
app/Jobs/ProcessProductImport.php:61: a manual for/fgetcsv loop with row-by-row updateOrCreate instead of chunked upsert or LazyCollection.
app/Http/Requests/StoreImportRequest.php:31-36: header parsing and BOM handling are duplicated between the FormRequest and the job's readHeader().
app/Models/Import.php:35: naming the relation errors() is ambiguous next to validation 'errors' terminology; rowErrors would be clearer.
app/Jobs/ProcessProductImport.php:42: forceFill is used to bypass a narrow fillable list instead of declaring the fields fillable.
strengths: Counts are consistent: duplicate SKUs are counted as updated, so created+updated+failed == total.
Uses apiResource()->only(), returns 202 Accepted, and dispatches with afterCommit().
Import::COLUMNS lives on the model, avoiding the job→FormRequest coupling.
Stock is capped at the unsignedInteger maximum and extra CSV columns are tolerated.
The job is simple and readable, with a clear rejectionReason() helper that uses Validator.
Tests include a 5MB boundary (accepted at exactly 5MB), quoted fields, extra columns, a failure path with no mail, and a mail content assertion.

v.rationale: Both suites pass (21 and 22 tests). Both implementations meet the core spec and use modern Laravel 12/13 idioms: attribute-based models and queued jobs, enum casts, a FormRequest with an after() header check, policies and JSON resources. impl-1 is built for production: it streams the file with a LazyCollection, writes products with a chunked bulk upsert, matches queue retry_after to the job timeout, records failure_reason, and fails deterministically when columns are missing. Its main defects are the duplicate-SKU count gap (created+updated+failed can be less than total) and the coupling of the job to a FormRequest constant. impl-2 is simpler and its counts always add up, and it returns 202 through apiResource. However, it does per-row updateOrCreate (N queries) under a 300s timeout without adjusting retry_after, returns null counts in the POST response, adds an always-true create policy, duplicates the header parsing, and retries deterministic failures. Overall the two are close; impl-1 ranks first for better scalability, failure handling and idiomatic collection use, despite its count-reporting bug.
